explanation: Dressage is French for 'training'. Equestrian events are among the few Olympic contests where women and men compete directly against each other.

claims.text: Dressage is an equestrian discipline at the Olympic Games.
Gymnastics, artistic swimming and figure skating have no event called dressage.
The word dressage is French for 'training'.
In Olympic equestrian events women and men compete against each other in the same events, which few Olympic sports allow.

evidence.restatement: Dressage is one of the three Olympic equestrian disciplines, alongside eventing and show jumping.
Gymnastics, artistic swimming and figure skating have no event called dressage.
The English word dressage is borrowed from French, from dresser, to train.
Olympic equestrian events have no gender split, so women and men compete in the same events, and the sport is commonly described as one of very few that do this.

claimResults.note: The word few is soft. Mixed doubles, mixed relays and sailing's mixed classes also put women and men in one event, so the claim is safest read as individual competition. It is defensible as hedged.

issues.note: The explanation says equestrian is among the few contests where women and men compete directly. That holds for individual events, but mixed doubles and mixed relays exist, so a pedant could object. The hedge among the few keeps it acceptable.
